2026-11-05FINCustoms TariffOrder Amending the United States Surtax Remission Order (2025)Order Amending the United States Surtax Remission Order (2025) in order to (1) extend remission to goods by adding (i) 205 products have been added to Schedule 2, which remit surtaxes to any importer in respect of products that have been determined to be in short supply;(ii) 6 products have been added to Schedule 3, which remits surtaxes to any importer in respect of products imported from the U.S. on a time-limited basis; (iii) 124 products have been added to Schedules 4 (importer-specific remission to September 1, 2025), 4.1 (importer specific remission within a specified time period), and 4.2 (importer specific remission starting September 8, 2026), which remit surtaxes for certain products imported from the U.S. due to exceptional circumstances; (2) extend and expand the scope of horizontal remission provided under the Order, (i) adding public education to eligible sectors under Section 1, pertaining to public health, public safety and national security; (ii) adding mining, quarrying or the extraction of oil or natural gas to the scope of domestic uses eligible or relief under Section 3; and, (iii) extending horizontal remission provided for under Sections 1, 2, 3 and 3.1 to June 30, 2028, with the exception of horizontal remission for steel goods under Section 3, which expired on January 31, 2026; and (3) recognize existing Canadian domestic market production capacity for certain products by restricting eligibility for the general horizonal remission provided under Section 3 by adding 19 products have been added to the new Schedule 7, which excludes certain tariff classifications from horizontal remission, due to the existence of domestic production capacity.Registration: SOR/2026-0235 Publication Date: 2026-11-18
subject: Order Amending the United States Surtax Remission Order (2025)
precis: Order Amending the United States Surtax Remission Order (2025) in order to (1) extend remission to goods by adding (i) 205 products have been added to Schedule 2, which remit surtaxes to any importer in respect of products that have been determined to be in short supply;(ii) 6 products have been added to Schedule 3, which remits surtaxes to any importer in respect of products imported from the U.S. on a time-limited basis; (iii) 124 products have been added to Schedules 4 (importer-specific remission to September 1, 2025), 4.1 (importer specific remission within a specified time period), and 4.2 (importer specific remission starting September 8, 2026), which remit surtaxes for certain products imported from the U.S. due to exceptional circumstances; (2) extend and expand the scope of horizontal remission provided under the Order, (i) adding public education to eligible sectors under Section 1, pertaining to public health, public safety and national security; (ii) adding mining, quarrying or the extraction of oil or natural gas to the scope of domestic uses eligible or relief under Section 3; and, (iii) extending horizontal remission provided for under Sections 1, 2, 3 and 3.1 to June 30, 2028, with the exception of horizontal remission for steel goods under Section 3, which expired on January 31, 2026; and (3) recognize existing Canadian domestic market production capacity for certain products by restricting eligibility for the general horizonal remission provided under Section 3 by adding 19 products have been added to the new Schedule 7, which excludes certain tariff classifications from horizontal remission, due to the existence of domestic production capacity.
